# Part 1: EDA on the original data (all headache types)

## General summary

```{r}
# Summarize the original data
load(here("data", "processed", "acupunc_full.RData"))
summary(acupunc_full)
```

## How many patients to each acupuncturist?

```{r}
# calculate and print
patients_per_acu_full <- acupunc_full %>% 
  # consider only patients who received acupuncture:
  filter(group == "acupuncture") %>%  
  group_by(acupuncturist) %>% summarize(n_patients = n())
kable(patients_per_acu_full)

# quantiles
quantile(patients_per_acu_full$n_patients)
```

12 total acupuncturists, ranging from 1 to 45 patients per acupuncturist.

## How many patients to each GP?

```{r}
# calculate and print
patients_per_gp_full <- acupunc_full %>% 
  group_by(gp) %>% summarize(n_patients = n())
kable(patients_per_gp_full)

# quantiles
quantile(patients_per_gp_full$n_patients)
```

36 total GPs, ranging from 1 to 43 patients per GP.

## How many patients by sex and headache type?

```{r}
# How many patients by sex and headache type?
sexheadache <- acupunc_full %>% 
  group_by(sex, migraine) %>% summarize(n())
kable(sexheadache)
```

# Part 2: EDA on the migraine-only data

## General summary

```{r}
# Summarize the data
load(here("data", "processed", "acupunc.RData"))
summary(acupunc)
```

## Acupuncturist breakdown: numbers of patients and GPs

```{r}
# How many patients and GPs to each acupuncturist?
patients_per_acu <- acupunc %>% 
  
  # consider only patients who received acupuncture
  filter(group == "acupuncture") %>%  
  
  # first, get number of patients per acupuncturist/GP combination
  group_by(acupuncturist, gp) %>% 
  summarize(obs = n()) %>% 
  
  # then collapse to number of patients and number of GPs
  group_by(acupuncturist) %>% 
  summarize(n_patients = sum(obs), n_GPs = n())

# View results
kable(patients_per_acu)
```

```{r}
# Quantiles of n_patients per acupuncturist
quantile(patients_per_acu$n_patients)
```

```{r}
# Quantiles of n_GPs per acupuncturist
quantile(patients_per_acu$n_GPs)
```

12 total acupuncturists, ranging from 1 to 42 patients per acupuncturist and 1 to 5 GPs per acupuncturist.

## GP breakdown: numbers of patients (total and per group) and assigned acupuncturist

```{r}
# How many patients to each GP?
patients_per_gp <- acupunc %>% 
  
  # get number of patients per GP and group, keeping the assigned acup'ist column
  rename(assigned_acupist = acupuncturist) %>% # more informative column name
  group_by(gp, assigned_acupist, group) %>% 
  summarize(n_patients = n()) %>%
  
  # create columns for number of patients per treatment group
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = n_patients) %>% 
  rename(n_patients_acup = acupuncture) %>% 
  rename(n_patients_control = control) %>% 
  # replace NAs with 0s:
  mutate(n_patients_acup = replace_na(n_patients_acup, 0)) %>% 
  mutate(n_patients_control = replace_na(n_patients_control, 0)) %>% 

  # create a column for total number of patients (per GP)
  mutate(n_patients_total = sum(n_patients_acup, n_patients_control))

# View results
kable(patients_per_gp)
```

```{r}
# Quantiles of total number of patients per GP
quantile(patients_per_gp$n_patients_total)
```

```{r}
# Quantiles of acupuncture group patients per GP
quantile(patients_per_gp$n_patients_acup)
```

```{r}
# Quantiles of control group patients per GP
quantile(patients_per_gp$n_patients_control)
```

35 total GPs, ranging from 1 to 41 total patients per GP, with 0-20 acupuncture patients and 0-21 control patients.

### Do GPs have an even split between acupuncture and control patients?

```{r}
patients_per_gp_uneven <- patients_per_gp %>% 
  # look at only GPs with an uneven split:
  filter(abs(n_patients_acup - n_patients_control) > 1) %>% 
  # which group is bigger?
  mutate(acup_greater = n_patients_acup > n_patients_control)

kable(patients_per_gp_uneven)
```

Most GPs have an even split between acupuncture and control patients (defined as a difference of 0 or 1 between the group sizes). However, of those with an uneven split, most have more patients in the acupuncture group. Overall, there are 11 more patients total in the acupuncture group than in the control group.

This 11-person difference is similar to the difference in groups before removing tension-type patients (9 more people in acupuncture). Furthermore, the publicly available data includes all 401 patients who were randomized, including those missing follow-up data. Therefore, I conclude that the disparity in acupuncture vs. control group numbers was present at the time of randomization and is not a result of my data processing.

## Breakdown by treatment group

### Categorical variable (patient sex)

```{r}
# patient count by sex and treatment group
sextreatment <- acupunc %>% 
  group_by(group, sex) %>% summarize(n = n())
kable(sextreatment)
```

```{r}
# patient sex percentages
print(paste("total % female:", round(100*(165+153)/(165+29+153+30), 2)))
print(paste("acupuncture % female:", round(100*(165)/(165+29), 2)))
print(paste("control % female:", round(100*(153)/(153+30), 2)))
```

### Numerical variables

```{r}
# Keep only numerical variables
acupunc_numerical <- acupunc %>% 
  select(group, age, chronicity, pk1, pk2, pk5, f1, f2, f5)

# Filter by treatment group
acupunc_numerical_acupuncture <- acupunc_numerical %>% 
  filter(group == "acupuncture")
acupunc_numerical_control <- acupunc_numerical %>% 
  filter(group == "control")

# Summarize the acupuncture patients
summary(acupunc_numerical_acupuncture)

# Summarize the control patients
summary(acupunc_numerical_control)
```
